expectations.text: All docstrings use triple double quotes ("""), none use ''' or single-line ' quotes
expectations.evidence: Every docstring opens/closes with """ (lines 1, 15, 27, 45, 63, 70, 95); grep finds no ''' or single-quote docstrings.

expectations.text: Module, class, and every public method have a docstring; multi-line docstrings have a one-sentence first line ending with a period, then a blank line
expectations.evidence: Module (line 1), class (line 15), __init__, schedule, next_ready_at, mark_failed, drain_ready all have docstrings. Multi-line ones start with one sentence ending in a period followed by a blank line, e.g. line 45 "Adds a task to the queue, ready immediately." then blank line 46. next_ready_at is single-line, which is exempt.

expectations.text: First lines are descriptive ("Schedules...", "Returns..."), not imperative ("Schedule...", "Return...")
next_ready_at documents the -1.0 sentinel meaning (task unknown/not pending)
expectations.evidence: Line 63: "Returns the task's ready time, or -1.0 if task_id is not pending."

expectations.text: mark_failed documents KeyError for unknown task_id (Raises:) and the None return meaning the task was dropped after exhausting attempts
expectations.evidence: Lines 81-82: "Raises:\n    KeyError: If task_id is not pending." Lines 78-79: "or None if it exhausted its attempts and was dropped."

expectations.text: drain_ready is documented with a Yields: section (not Returns:) and mentions that drained tasks are removed from the queue
expectations.evidence: Lines 100-102: "Yields:\n    (task_id, payload) pairs for each ready task; yielded tasks are removed from the queue." No Returns: section.

expectations.text: schedule's Returns: explains the True/False semantics (False = task_id already pending, call ignored)
expectations.evidence: Line 54: "True if the task was added, False if task_id is already pending."

expectations.text: Args: sections list each parameter with expected types (code has no annotations) and consistent continuation indentation
expectations.evidence: Continuation indentation is consistent, but no Args entry states a type: line 48 "task_id: Unique identifier for the task.", line 30 "max_attempts: Failures allowed before a task is dropped" — no int/float/str/Hashable type given for any parameter despite the unannotated code.

expectations.text: No comments that merely restate the code (e.g. '# increment attempts' style)
expectations.evidence: Only three comments, all informative: line 41 "# Maps task_id to [payload, failure_count, ready_at]." (documents opaque list layout), line 90 "# Exponential backoff: base_delay doubles with each failure." (explains the formula's intent). No restating comments.

expectations.text: Free prose of every docstring (summary line plus expanded description, excluding Args:/Returns:/Raises: sections) is at most 3 sentences
expectations.evidence: Module: 1 sentence + example intro; class: 2 sentences (lines 15-18); __init__, schedule, next_ready_at, mark_failed, drain_ready: 1 sentence of prose each. All at most 3.

expectations.text: Each Args:/Returns:/Raises: entry is a single short sentence (allow two for mark_failed's dual None semantics)
expectations.evidence: Every entry is one sentence, e.g. line 54 Returns, line 30-31 "Failures allowed before a task is dropped; must be >= 1.", mark_failed Returns (lines 78-79) is a single sentence covering both outcomes.

expectations.text: No usage-example blocks or example output listings anywhere in the file
expectations.evidence: Module docstring lines 3-8 contain "Typical usage example:" followed by a code block ("queue = RetryQueue(max_attempts=3)" etc.).
